form.freeNote: Without a key, {name}'s bot answers up to {limit, number} messages a day for free (default model: {model}). If a factual question is not covered by its knowledge, it does not make something up: it hands off with “{holding}” and marks the conversation “{badge}” in the Inbox. Add your own API key to choose the model and answer without a limit. You are billed through your key.

budget.noLimit: Replies run on your key with no limit. You are billed through that key.
budget.freeLimit: Right now up to {limit, number} replies a day are free.
budget.autoLimit: Right now up to {limit, number} replies a day are sent automatically.
budget.upgrade: Add a {provider} key to answer with no limit. You are billed through that key.

fields.customNote: You can use a model that is not on the list. We just cannot check the name when you save, so a wrong name shows up as a failure on the first reply.
fields.keyNote: Before saving, we ask {provider} once to confirm the key actually works. After saving only the last 4 characters are shown, and the original never appears on any screen again.

models.claude-sonnet-5: Balance of speed and quality · input $2 / 1M

purposes.intro: {name}'s bot does a different job at each step of the loop. The beta is on, so Feedloop pays for organizing feedback and creating fix PRs. All four steps run even if you add no key.
purposes.open: You can run this on your own key
purposes.lockedLabel: {title} — cannot be configured during the beta
purposes.lockedKey: API key — not needed for now

reply.title: Answer customers
reply.what: When a visitor talks to the widget or a channel, it answers on the spot. A person cannot be kept waiting, so it has to finish within 10 seconds.
reply.guide: A fast, cheap model fits here. As the knowledge grows, though, we have seen cheaper models miss the rule of handing off to the owner instead of making things up.

organize.title: Organize feedback
organize.what: Sorts incoming feedback into categories and groups the same problems. It reads dozens of items at once.
organize.guide: This step reads far more at once than answering does, so cheaper models are more likely to miss things.

fix.title: Create fix PRs
fix.what: Turns a grouped problem into an actual code fix (a PR). It reads the repository and rewrites code, the heaviest job of all.
fix.guide: It reads code and rewrites it directly, so this step needs the best model.

closing.what: Sends what was fixed back to the person who first reported it. It uses fixed wording, so it hardly uses AI.
